q: Which is NOT a projective technique?
exp: Questionnaires are objective tests; projective tests use ambiguous stimuli.

q: Why is sex education considered important in schools?
options: It gives correct scientific knowledge and removes myths and misconceptions
It is useful only for adults
exp: Accurate information helps adolescents develop healthy attitudes.

q: A 'backward child' as defined by Burt is one whose
options: educational attainment is below that of the age group
exp: Burt defined backwardness in terms of attainment lagging behind age.

q: For a child with hearing impairment, the teacher should
options: seat the child at the back
seat the child in front and use visual aids and clear lip-visible speech
speak very loudly while facing the board
exp: Front seating and visual support help communication.

q: Which of the following is NOT a role of a teacher in a school guidance programme?
exp: A teacher is not a medical professional.

q: Seating students in a U-shape arrangement mainly encourages
exp: A U-shape lets the teacher and students see each other easily.

q: Which of the following is NOT associated with Gandhi's educational thought?
options: Heavy emphasis on English medium and bookish knowledge
exp: Gandhi opposed an education that was bookish and in a foreign language.

q: Which book was written by Sri Aurobindo?
exp: The Life Divine is Aurobindo's major philosophical work.

q: Which of the following is an individual aim of education?
exp: Individual aims focus on developing each learner's potential.

q: According to the usual norm under RTE rules, a primary school should be within
exp: The model rules specify within 1 km for classes I-V and 3 km for classes VI-VIII.

q: Approximately how long does the prenatal stage of human development last?
options: About 280 days from conception to birth
exp: The prenatal period is roughly 266-280 days, i.e., nine months.

q: Seriation (arranging sticks from shortest to longest) becomes possible in the
exp: Logical operations on concrete objects such as ordering and classifying emerge at 7-11 years.

q: Which teaching strategy is MOST in line with Vygotsky?
options: Collaborative group work with guidance from the teacher
exp: Learning through guided social interaction is central to his theory.

q: According to Kohlberg, most adults reach which level?
exp: Most adolescents and adults reason at the conventional level; postconventional reasoning is less common.

q: The main difference between Freud's and Erikson's theories is that Erikson emphasised
options: social and cultural influences across the whole life span
exp: Erikson stressed psychosocial crises through life rather than sexual drives in childhood.

q: Watson and Rayner's 'Little Albert' experiment demonstrated the
exp: A fear of a white rat was conditioned by pairing it with a loud noise.

q: Which theory is most closely linked to the idea of 'learning by insight' and 'perceptual organisation'?
exp: Wertheimer, Kohler and Koffka stressed insight and perception of the whole.

q: Hull's drive-reduction theory holds that behaviour is motivated by
exp: Hull said an unsatisfied need creates a drive and drive reduction reinforces behaviour.

q: The concept of Emotional Intelligence was popularised by
exp: Goleman popularised it after Salovey and Mayer introduced the term.

q: The stage in which the creator is not consciously working on the problem but the mind continues to process it is
exp: In incubation, unconscious processing occurs before the sudden insight.

q: Kretschmer classified people by body build into
exp: Kretschmer's classification is pyknic, athletic and asthenic.

q: Statement I: Adolescents need independence. Statement II: They also need guidance from adults. Which is correct?
exp: Adolescents seek autonomy but still require supportive guidance.

q: The statement 'No two persons are exactly alike' is called the
exp: It is the basic principle of individual differences.

q: Which of these children is also referred to as 'twice exceptional'?
options: A gifted child who also has a learning disability
exp: Twice exceptional learners have both high ability and a disability.

q: Guidance mainly aims at
options: helping an individual to help himself
doing the individual's work for him
exp: Guidance develops self-direction and self-understanding.

q: Effective teachers handle misbehaviour mainly by
options: understanding its cause and responding calmly
sending all students to the principal
exp: Calm, cause-based responses solve problems more permanently.

q: Tagore's idea of education aimed at
options: harmony between the individual, society and nature, and international understanding
exp: Tagore wanted a universal humanism with global outlook.

q: Vivekananda held that religion in education should be
options: universal and aimed at realising the divinity within
exp: He emphasised the essential unity of all religions.

q: Which of the following is a feature of progressive education?
exp: Progressivism, influenced by Dewey, puts the child at the centre.

q: Which of the following is true about the RTE Act?
options: It prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment of children
It applies only to private schools
exp: Section 17 prohibits corporal punishment and mental harassment.
